title: Research audit: ordered-subset bounds allow quadratic interval amplification
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Adversarial mathematical audit / scoped negative result; no new kappa.**

The retained PR905 precision proof bounds an interval by two prefix bounds. This package proves that the resulting quadratic dependence on an ordered-subset norm budget cannot be replaced by a linear dependence for general noncommuting factors, even with invertible factors and a disturbance on a real leaf destination.

In the unchanged PR628 seven-factor word, every ordered subset product has norm at most `G=M`, but the interval `[13,27)` has diagonal block `I-JD` with norm `1+M^2`. The complete ideal word has norm two and restores all dirty arrays. The README supplies an exact parametric proof for every real `M>=1`. A smaller four-factor example distinguishes arbitrary register perturbations from actual leaf-destination support.

This is evidence for retaining the generic conservative bound, not a bug in PR905 or a lower bound on the working precision of its cyclic leaves. The family violates their common-operator/commutation assumption. No actual deterministic rounding-failure trace, physical implementation, supplier admission, full theorem verification or new exponent is claimed.

## Task and overlap

Base: `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`. Assignment seed **64**, adversarial audit; the `uniform-transfer-audit` card is refined to this exact two-cut implication. Only `research/dirty-interval-propagator-audit/` is added.

The source pins are PR628 `0768f97d06c623b8211e651543c66135796b62bf`, PR905 `aab6c0b8f4574cb36285ab5dab3fcfad0cd2b69e`, and PR877 `80a60c0da2b916798167deb0ce3a5ef22fda147a`; consumed bytes also have base Git-blob and SHA256 bindings. Current main was refreshed to `dd6403f774a0891093a006ae9716c02e371b1fdb`; consumed sources and selected certificate are unchanged from the experiment base.

The final textual overlap refresh covered all **843 open PRs** and **16 discussion records**, with complete pagination reported and no warnings. Nearest overlap is [PR1085](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1085), which sharpens prefix coefficients. This contribution instead gives an explicit interval obstruction and the distinction between arbitrary and leaf-supported perturbations. PR1054, PR1093 and PR1211 cover different accuracy or tape obligations. No literature-priority claim is made. The local claim, bounded domain and coverage are in TASK.json; no pinned sprint issue was present.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-interval-propagator-audit
```

Expected: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/dirty-interval-propagator-audit outcome=negative-result`.

- All **9,772** nonempty intervals through eight factors, both signs; **9,342** preceding-leaf destination columns. The first unordered monomial appears at four factors generally and seven for destination-supported inputs.
- **26** literal dispatcher comparisons; **16** exact dense cases; independent full-matrix multiplication, Gauss-Jordan two-cut reconstruction and dirty vector trajectories.
- Positive prefix/inverse-prefix controls at **446** boundaries; **six** mathematical separation controls; **seven** passing package tests, including source/receipt faults and read-only relocation.
- Python **3.12.13** isolated optimized replay matches the receipt generated under **3.14.6**. All **25** selected-record tests pass. Canonical mathematical receipt SHA256: `1cd6367958cd6eb107840c79190409c22ac11aad9a7d9278b4b4ed5a2f2d98ad`.

The finite census supports the written argument; it is not an all-size formal proof. The selected cold replay, repository-wide historical suites and hosted CI were not run for this local scoped package.

Prepared for **Hanson Sun (@bbMisk)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in research, proof, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0; predecessor files and attribution remain unchanged. No independent human or proof-assistant review is claimed.

## Open next questions

The README/TASK ask whether the common-operator case admits a linear-in-G interval bound. The finite census has only squarefree monomials through eight factors; an induction over endpoint subcalls, including reused deeper scratch, is still needed. This obstruction deliberately leaves that possible route to a tighter cyclic precision estimate open.
